Monday, April 20, 2020  7:00 PM  Teleconference

Pursuant to the Governor's Executive Order N-29-20, Park and Activities Commission Members will be
participating via teleconference.

- Commission meeting videos are live-streamed on the City’s website at www.rhe.city and available for viewing.

- Members of the public may listen to the meeting live by calling: (1-669-900-6833) from any phone, Meeting ID:
971 9086 4115 , Meeting Password: 980063. (Please note you will not have the ability to speak using the call-in
option from a phone line.)

- Public correspondence may be emailed to the Cynthia Morquecho, Community Services Supervisor at
cynthiam@rollinghillsestatesca.gov. Emails received before 5:00 p.m. the night of the meeting will be forwarded
to the Commission for their consideration and included as part of the record.

- Members of the public may comment online using eComment on the “Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos”
page of the City’s website (www.rhe.city/MeetingAgendas). Once the agenda is published, there will be an
“eComment” button next to the linked agenda under "Upcoming Events". Follow this link to the City’s SpeakUp
page. After you register, you may comment on any item on that particular agenda. These comments can be seen
by the public, will be considered by the Commission and become part of the record.

- Members of the public who wish to speak during this meeting may join the Zoom meeting by accessing the
Zoom app from a computer (downloaded at Zoom.com) or tablet or phone (downloaded in the App Store), by
entering the following credentials: Meeting ID: 971 9086 4115 , Meeting Password: 980063

Members of the public who join the Zoom meeting will not have video, and may request to speak using the
following process: After joining the Zoom meeting, if you wish to speak, please select the "raise hand" option at
the lower portion of your screen. The City Clerk will send you a chat message to identify which item on the
agenda you would like to speak on and will unmute your mic at the appropriate time.

Agenda reports and other disclosable public records relating to each agenda item are available on the City's
website under Meeting Agendas, Minutes & Videos at www.rhe.city.

MINUTES
  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING
  APRIL 20, 2020

  The Park and Activities Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order at 7:07

  1.  CALL MEETING TO ORDER

  2.  SALUTE TO THE FLAG

  CHAIR PERSICHINA led those present in the Pledge of Allegiance.

  3.  ROLL CALL

  COMMISSIONERS PRESENT:  Perichina, Pope,  Bain,  Romanelli,  Ciarolla,
  McCormick, Retz

  COMMISSIONERS ABSENT:  None

  STAFF PRESENT:  Alexa Davis, Assistant City Manager (ACM)
  Cynthia Morquecho, Comm. Services Supervisor
  Daniel A-Haja, Community Services Coordinator
  Lauren Pettit, City Clerk

  4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ADJOURNED DRAFT MINUTES OF

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that her comment on fence repairs pertained to Highridge

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER POPE to:

  APPROVE THE PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF
  FEBRUARY 18, 2020 AS CORRECTED.

DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  1
APRIL 20, 2020
   6.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A. INSTALLATION LOCATION OF ARMENIAN GENOCIDE MEMORIAL

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided a brief overview per
  the agenda material.

  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN provided further details of the memorial. The memorial
  is both commemoration to the Armenian genocide and to genocides across the world. The
  memorial would be one of the few memorials on public property of its kind. COUNCIL
  MEMBER ZERUNYAN provided an overview of the history and purpose of the memorial’s
  message. COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN mentioned his personal heritage to those of
  the genocide. The plaque will depict a woman carrying her child on her back which derives
  from a previous campaign originally established by the American Red Cross. The location
  of the memorial is proposed to be near the vegetation next to the existing plaque. The
  memorial is planned to be a six-foot-tall rock with the two foot by three foot plaque of the
  woman and child along with a smaller plaque below about one square foot in size with
  verbiage about the memorial. The estimated cost is about $20,000-$25,000 and will be
  funded by donations with any extra donated funds benefitting the Pepper Tree Foundation.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ clarified that funding would be solicited through the Pepper Tree
  Foundation, and any additional funds raised will go to the Pepper Tree Foundation.
  COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN confirmed.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN asked if there needed to be a signing off from the original artist of
  the plaque to have the more detailed larger plaque up for the memorial. The plaque also
  has no date indicating the date it was originally commemorated. COUNCIL MEMBER
  ZERUNYAN responded that he intended to use the City website to promote the Relief
  Foundation by educating the public about the artist and memorial.

  VICE CHAIR POPE asked if the current plaque near the proposed memorial will need to
  be moved. COUNCIL MEMBER ZERUNYAN noted it can be moved to a more prominent
  location which will not interfere with the memorial.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ made a motion, seconded by VICE CHAIR POPE to:

  APPROVE THE PLAQUE AND THE STAFF REPORT AS PRESENTED.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA REQUESTED A ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES: Persichina, Pope, Ciarolla, Bain, McCormick, Retz, & Romanelli
  NAYES: None
  ABSENT : None

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  B. GRANT APPLICATION FOR MONTICILLO ENTRYWAY

DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  2
APRIL 20, 2020
   COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided a brief overview
  per the agenda material.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if the HOA is using an approved City Contractor then only
  one quote would need to be provided. ACM DAVIS confirmed.

  COMMISSIONER BAIN noted that the invoice included the cost of business license
  for $154 which is charged to the HOA. RESIDENT ED MOHR of the Montecillo HOA
  stated California Banner and Sign did not have a current business license with the City
  and the HOA offered to include it in total cost so the company could complete the
  installation. COMMISSIONER RETZ noted this cost was for businesses to pay and
  that the HOA should not be responsible for the fee. ACM DAVIS noted that California
  Banner and Signs do not do installations within the City and that this would be the only
  job they would do within the City. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked what the
  balance of funds would be left after this project. ACM DAVIS noted that the original
  budget was $5,000 but was re-adjusted to $2,500 during the mid-year review due to
  limited requests resulting in no remaining funds if this request was granted

  VICE CHAIR POPE made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER RETZ to:

  APPROVE STAFF RECOMMENDATION FOR THE $2,500 IN STREET
  ENTRYWAY BEAUTIFICATION GRANT FUNDS FOR THE MONTECILLO HOA
  STREET ENTRYWAY GRANT APPLICATION.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA REQUESTED A ROLL CALL VOTE:

  AYES: Persichina, Pope, Ciarolla, Bain, McCormick, Retz, & Romanelli
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT :  None

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.

  7.  COMMISSION ITEMS (VERBAL REPORT)

  A.  ADOPT-A-PARK REPORTS (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMISSIONER BAIN stated that Highridge Park was nearly empty of patrons and
  commended maintenance staff on their work. COMMISSIONER BAIN asked when
  fencing repair will occur. COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO
  responded maintenance staff will be notified of needed repairs; funds from an ongoing
  grant will fund the fence repair. The grant was approved but additional documents need
  to be submitted to the grant manager and funds are expected to come soon.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted fencing on Palos Verdes Drive East about 500 yards
  before Palos Verdes Drive North on left side of the street needed repair. Fencing
  westbound on Dapplegray Lane also needed repair. ACM DAVIS noted staff was aware
  and will be notified regarding Palos Verdes Drive East.

DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  3
APRIL 20, 2020
   COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted the walking trail on Palos Verdes Drive North
  heading towards Silver Spur had posts damaged on the asphalt side of the trail. ACM
  DAVIS noted maintenance was aware and will be repairing.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if field rental fees will be refunded to the those who paid early
  in the calendar year. ACM DAVIS noted staff is looking at the issue due to the COVID-19
  situation staff is researching viable options such as refunds.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA received and filed.

  8.  STAFF ITEMS

  A.  COVID-19 UPDATE (VERBAL REPORT)

  ACM Davis reported the Safer at Home order has been extended to May 15 and essential
  businesses are still operating albeit in modified ways. City Hall remains closed to the
  public, but staff is still working from home. Per Los Angeles County order, recreational
  facilities such as tennis courts and basketball courts remain closed to the public along with
  sport fields to organized activities. Trails and parks are open to passive use though no
  events or training is allowed. The Sheriff have increased patrols of the parks along with
  Staff which have aided in keeping park gathering numbers down. The City is providing
  updates daily on multiple platforms including the City website. ACM Davis added that, the
  public is now required to wear a face covering mask when entering buildings and essential
  work areas though not required if taking a walk or maintaining social distancing. All
  workers and essential business workers are required to wear face coverings in order to
  operate business in the County. City staff is still operating outdoors such as landscaping
  and tree trimming while using masks. COMMISSIONERS ROMANELLI and RETZ
  commended the efforts of City Staff through this difficult time.

  B.  UPCOMING CITY EVENTS (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO asked for Committee guidance
  on the upcoming Mayor’s Breakfast Ride and suggested postponing the event. She
  reported that the Boy Scouts unfortunately will not be able to host the pancake portion of
  the event. With the future limitations on group gatherings, events such as Tracy Austin
  Doubles Tennis Tournament may not have enough time to receive sponsorship funding.
  Staff have reached out to Tracy Austin to explore a plan for that event. The Hills Are Alive
  event is still slated for August though can be postponed to Fall if necessary. The Race
  Director advance has been lowered from $4,000 to $2,000 prior to the event as a non-
  refundable payment to the Race Director to consider options of postponing or canceling
  the event.

  COMMISSIONER RETZ noted the Mayor’s Ride lends itself to the Social Distancing order
  but asked what alternative breakfast there could be. ACM Davis noted that pre-packaged
  food can be used. COMMISSIONER RETZ suggested a tentative date. COMMUNITY
  SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted a suggested date of September or
  October. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA asked if the City Celebration in September would
  still be going on at that time. COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO
DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  4
APRIL 20, 2020
   responded that the event will still take place on the 26th and the ride can take place earlier
  in the month. ACM DAVIS noted that the Portuguese Bend Horse show may also take
  place around that time and staff will consider planning around that. COMMISSIONER
  BAIN noted that some cities that have scheduled events may re-infect the population with
  COVID-19 but would be concerned about close proximity events including children such
  as the City Celebration event. ACM DAVIS suggested staff re-evaluate the situation in
  June or July as more information comes out to re-assess the event so specific planning is
  not required yet. Staff is asking whether to postpone or cancel the Ride per Commission
  suggestion. If postponed, is Fall an acceptable time to reschedule. CHAIR PERSICHINA
  suggests postponing the Ride and going month by month on deciding what to do with the
  events. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked how much time is needed to coordinate
  such events. COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR noted most events that require
  sponsorship need about 3 to 4 months of preparation but smaller events such as the Ride
  can take a month to plan. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggested subtracting the
  breakfast until a vaccine is available and to be conservative when deciding.
  COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated the breakfast is the main attraction of the event but
  since social distancing cannot be maintained, the ride may be combined with part of
  another major event like the Tracy Austin Doubles Tournament or the Hills Are Alive Race.
  VICE CHAIR POPE asked how many riders attend the event. SUPERVISOR
  MORQUECHO noted 60 to 80 riders with approximately ten dignitaries. VICE CHAIR
  POPE noted the event could be a positive sign for the City once the gatherings are allowed
  to take place again. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA mentioned that the equestrian
  community was heavily involved in last year’s event. She asked if staff could provide
  refreshments for riders at the beginning of the event in Chandler Park and stated that the
  event can take place any time during the year. ACM DAVIS noted the Equestrian
  Committee can be engaged in May or June for input. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA noted
  the dignitaries that attended in the past such as Al Muratsuchi and Janice Hahn.
  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted the input and will try to postpone the event and
  consult the Equestrian Committee. ACM DAVIS mentioned the Movie Nights will also be
  affected and asked the Commission for guidance. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI stated
  that the June movie should be postponed as well and that Movie Nights should follow the
  direction of the other special events. SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted the suggestion
  and added the June Movie Night will be canceled with future review for July and August
  events.

  C.  VIRTUAL RECREATION SITE (VERBAL REPORT)

  COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR AHAJA highlighted the addition of a Virtual
  Recreation on the City website for those affected by the COVID-19. The site includes
  City-wide activities such as the most recent Easter Egg Hunt. COMMUNITY SERVICES
  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted the success of the activity suggested by VICE
  CHAIR POPE. The winner of the event won a $25 gift card from the local Red Onion.
  COMMUNITY SERVICES COORDINATOR AHAJA noted that the City is hosting a virtual
  Earth Day.
  D.  PROPOSED PARK TOURS SCHEDULE
  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO asked the Commission would
  like tours to take place individually and discussed over Zoom video conference or to make
  up the May visits and do two park site visits in August to make up for missing one. CHAIR
DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  5
APRIL 20, 2020
   PERSICHINA suggests postponing walking the parks until July and that the Commission
  could add multiple parks per visit to catch up through September. He added that Highridge
  Park should be done by itself.
  9.  ADJOURN TO THE PEPPER TREE FOUNDATION ADISORY COMMITTEE MEETING

  A.  2020 HILLS ARE ALIVE RACE CONSULTANT AGREEMENT
  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO provided a brief overview per
  the agenda material. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted that the Race Subcommittee
  wanted to incentivize Michael Hogue to increase participation and noted that there was no
  incentive in the agreement. COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO
  noted it was a part conversation but was not included in the contract, it can be added if
  desired by the Commission, COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI noted staff was capable of
  operating the event without the Race Director per past meetings. COVID-19 may hold it
  unfair to require the Race Director to increase the number of participants but remains
  germane to the subject. ACM DAVIS noted some edits that provide more accountability
  to the Race Director including sponsorship duties. COMMISSIONER RETZ noted the
  termination clause should be edited to provide more clarification. COMMUNITY
  SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO will work with the City Attorney, but noted
  under the draft agreement the $2,000 is to be paid to the Race Director whether the event
  runs or not. ACM DAVIS noted the $2,000 is to be paid after the agreement is agreed
  upon by the City. The reasons for cancellation will be clarified. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI asked what the reasons the Race Director would have to cancel the event
  on their behalf. COMMISSIONER BAIN noted that the Race Director would be
  responsible for television commercials and wondered if that was viable. ACM DAVIS
  responded that in the past commercials were provided and are still available to implement
  at no cost from the local government channel. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK asked
  how much the Race Director receives compared to the Pepper Tree Foundation.
  COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO responded that each party
  receives about $9,500 in funds each. CHAIR PERSICHINA asked if the agreement has
  a deadline. ACM DAVIS noted that for an August event date, May would still work to have
  an agreement agreed upon due to the COVID-19 situation. COMMUNITY SERVICES
  SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO noted that no finalized agreement has been sent out to
  Michael Hogue yet. COMMISSIONER RETZ noted the possibility of postponing the event
  until COVID-19 issues become clearer. COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI asked how
  urgent this agreement was for Michael Hogue. COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR
  MORQUECHO stated that typically the agreement is approved in March. Staff has
  continuously updating Michael Hogue on the status of the agreement. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI noted this would be an opportunity to include incentives such as a 10%
  increase in participation. COMMISSIONER CIAROLLA noted the race promoter may not
  have been incentivized to increase the participation for the event. S

  ACM DAVIS stated that she will request the City Attorney to review suggestions for
  Commission consideration May. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK stated that 50% of
  entry fees is very generous and that it may not be an incentive issue but a performance
  issue with the Race Director. COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO
  noted that incentives would be helpful in increasing participation. COMMUNITY
  SERVICES COORDINATOR AHAJA added in comparison that other City events such as
DRAFT PARK AND ATIVITIES MEETING MINUTES  6
APRIL 20, 2020
   the Tracy Austin Doubles Tournament pay the tournament director approximately $1,000
  for a three day event. COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO
  responded that the Race Director is also responsible for bringing in sponsorships which
  differs from the tournament director tasks. ACM DAVIS noted that incentives should be
  specified such as the 10% participant increase. COMMISIONER ROMANELLI responded
  that the goals must be tangible and measurable. CHAIR PERSICHINA noted the
  motivating factor was 50% of sponsorships and race entries. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI suggested taking away the sponsorship incentives but increase participant
  incentives. COMMUNITY SERVICES SUPERVISOR MORQUECHO suggested bringing
  these changes to the City Attorney and then back to the Subcommittee for review before
  coming back to Commission for approval. COMMISSIONER MCCORMICK suggested
  not increasing the number of runners due to the pandemic but asked if we should rather
  have the City staff run the event by themselves this year. ACM DAVIS noted staff can run
  the event by themselves and based on guidance from the Commission but know that
  Michael Hogue is eager to continue his partnership with the City. COMMISSIONER
  ROMANELLI noted City staff can run the event as in previous years.

  CHAIR PERSICHINA made a motion, seconded by COMMISSIONER ROMANELLI to:

  HAVE STAFF REVISE THE AGREEMENT TO INCLUDE EDITS APPROVED BY
  THE CITY ATTORNEY FOR COMMISSION APPROVAL IN MAY.

  There being no objection, CHAIR PERSICHINA so ordered.
